summary: The data shows a fully reactive looping strategy with zero announced carbohydrates over the 14-day period. The algorithm relies entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) and Dynamic ISF to manage glucose spikes, leading to aggressive insulin stacking due to exceptionally loose safety limits. This stacked insulin routinely causes significant overnight hypoglycemia as it catches up to an overly aggressive 90 mg/dL nighttime target.
education: Unannounced meals force the closed-loop system to react only after glucose has already spiked, requiring much more insulin to bring glucose down than a prebolus would.

Extremely high Max IOB (25 U) and Max Basal (12 U/h) limits allow the pump to deliver massive amounts of insulin during a spike, which often remains active long after the meal's carbohydrates have finished absorbing.
A nighttime target of 90 mg/dL leaves no safety buffer against leftover active insulin, making nocturnal hypoglycemia highly likely if evening meals are unannounced.
strengths: Excellent CGM coverage at 98.7% with minimal data gaps.
The system is actively maintaining closed-loop status and responding dynamically to glucose changes.
Morning fasting glucose frequently returns to range after nocturnal lows are resolved.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
GLP-1 medications can significantly delay gastric emptying, which alters carbohydrate absorption profiles. Monitor closely when adjusting insulin timing.
An overnight target of 90 mg/dL combined with 25 U of Max IOB poses a severe hypoglycemia risk. Discuss raising targets and restricting safety limits with your care team immediately.

analysis_steps.evidence: 98.7% CGM coverage, 3995 entries, max gap 65 minutes. 655 insulin entries. 0 carbohydrate entries recorded (total_carbs_g: 0).
analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry and CGM cadence are excellent, but the complete absence of logged carbohydrates dictates that glucose excursions are managed entirely unannounced.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero recorded carbs prevents classical analysis of Carbohydrate Ratios (CR) and meal bolus timing.

analysis_steps.evidence: Time Below Range (TBR) is 5.1%, peaking at 18.5% at 01:00, 10.1% at 02:00, and 15.3% at 19:00. Time Above Range peaks mid-day (14:00-17:00 at 22-32%).
analysis_steps.findings: Significant nocturnal hypoglycemia risk exists. High variability suggests under-treatment of mid-day glucose spikes followed by aggressive late-day and overnight over-correction.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot separate daytime highs into unannounced meal timing versus basal deficits.

analysis_steps.evidence: Profile targets step down to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 and remain at 90 mg/dL until 08:00. TBR accelerates in the evening and stays high through the night.
analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL target overnight is highly aggressive and leaves almost no safety buffer against dynamic ISF variations or leftover active insulin, directly contributing to severe nocturnal TBR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Difficult to fully isolate baseline basal needs in the late evening due to UAM-driven IOB from unannounced evening meals.

analysis_steps.evidence: A flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is in the profile, but loop logs reveal Dosing Sensitivity is dynamically scaled down to ~36 mg/dL/U. CR changes dynamically throughout the day but is applied strictly by UAM.
analysis_steps.findings: The system's aggressive dynamic ISF responses, combined with a 90 mg/dL target, amplify the risk of over-delivery for any perceived glucose rise. CR evaluation is entirely mathematical because no manual carbs are entered.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot assess real-world CR accuracy without meal entries.

analysis_steps.evidence: uam_enabled=true and smb_always_enabled=true are active. Loop logs confirm UAM is heavily engaged (e.g., UAM Boost 1/2).
analysis_steps.findings: The system is functioning as a fully closed-loop, reactive system without manual meal announcements. Mid-day TAR is a direct consequence of this trailing response.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal timing data to evaluate whether UAM duration matches actual meal absorption.

analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour is 12 U/h. max_iob_units is 25 U. dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true (70% adjustment factor) is aggressively modulating ISF based on BG momentum.
analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are exceptionally loose. The algorithm interprets sudden post-prandial BG spikes as massive temporary insulin resistance, delivering large volumes of insulin. Delayed IOB carries over, colliding with the overly tight 90 mg/dL target.

The user does not manually announce meals. This purely reactive approach allows glucose to spike significantly before triggering massive, delayed UAM and Dynamic ISF insulin responses that crash glucose later.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True meal times, composition, and carbohydrate amounts are unknown.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not utilized. UAM is the sole mechanism handling all carbohydrate absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot evaluate actual carbohydrate absorption times without carb entries.

analysis_steps.evidence: Target profile of 90 mg/dL combined with unannounced meals, Max IOB of 25 U, and Max Basal of 12 U/h creates severe nighttime lows (18.5% TBR at 01:00).
analysis_steps.findings: The immediate priority must be resolving the nocturnal hypoglycemia. This requires raising the overnight target to create a safety buffer and severely restricting the maximum allowed basal and IOB limits to prevent massive insulin stacking during unannounced meals.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Underlying CR and Basal needs cannot be verified until carbs are logged and extreme reactive IOB is restricted.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target for Safety
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL leaves no safety buffer for delayed insulin absorption from unannounced meals, resulting in 18.5% time below range at 01:00.

recommendations.title: Restrict Max IOB and Max Basal
recommendations.description: Current safety limits (12 U/h basal, 25 U IOB) are excessively loose for a profile with a peak basal rate of 0.8 U/h, allowing massive insulin stacking during reactive UAM delivery.

recommendations.title: Begin Logging Carbohydrates
recommendations.description: Zero logged carbs forces the algorithm to chase spikes reactively. Announcing meals will allow prebolusing, significantly reducing mid-day spikes and preventing the massive reactive insulin deliveries that crash blood glucose overnight.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides insufficient safety buffer against active insulin stacked during late-evening unannounced meals, driving severe nocturnal hypoglycemia (18.5% TBR at 01:00).
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight glucose for 3 days after raising the target to 100 mg/dL to ensure TBR drops below 4%.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 00:00 and 23:00 target segments to 100 mg/dL to reduce nocturnal hypoglycemia risk.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: 12 U/h and 25 U are excessively high for a profile with a max scheduled basal of 0.8 U/h, allowing massive insulin stacking during unannounced meals that directly causes overnight crashes.
Dynamic ISF is functioning as expected given the massive glucose momentum generated by unannounced meals. Tightening safety limits will organically constrain its behavior.

implementation_steps: Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 Target profile segments to 100 mg/dL to immediately mitigate severe nocturnal hypoglycemia risk.
Reduce AAPS max_basal_u_per_hour to 2.5 U/h and max_iob_units to 7 U to prevent dangerous insulin stacking during reactive UAM delivery.
Begin logging all meals with carbohydrate amounts and exact timestamps in the AAPS app.
Once meals are logged consistently for 3-5 days, review the data to assess baseline Carbohydrate Ratios (CR) and actual insulin absorption patterns.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero carbohydrate entries dictate that the system manages all meals completely reactively via UAM. This causes massive mid-day spikes, followed by excessive, trailing insulin delivery that crashes glucose overnight.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Begin manually entering carbohydrates into the system and executing a standard prebolus to align insulin action with food absorption, reducing both daytime spikes and nighttime crashes.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log exact carbohydrate amounts and timestamps for at least 3-5 days to generate actionable CR and absorption data.
